variable.description: (Required) Creates a data sync table for the database related to theprovided value.

request.description: Creates a new data sync table with the given data sync type. This will technically create a table, but it's synchronized with the provided data sync information. This means that some fields related to it will automatically be created and will be read-only.

variable.description: (Required) Updates the order of the tables in the database related to the provided value.

request.description: Changes the order of the provided table ids to the matching position that the id has in the list. If the authorized user does not belong to the workspace it will be ignored. The order of the not provided tables will be set to `0`.

variable.description: (Required) Returns only tables that are related to the provided value.

request.description: Lists all the tables that are in the database related to the `database_id` parameter if the user has access to the database's workspace. A table is exactly as the name suggests. It can hold multiple fields, each having their own type and multiple rows. They can be added via the **create_database_table_field** and **create_database_table_row** endpoints.

request.description:
Creates synchronously a new table for the database related to the provided `database_id` parameter if the authorized user has access to the database's workspace.

As an alternative you can use the `create_async_database_table` for better performances and importing bigger files.
